html:
The conversion of the rulers of Kanem, north and east of Lake Chad, to Islam in the late 11th century, under the king Hummay, founder of the Sayfawa dynasty.

Kanem's kings, called mai, grew rich by selling slaves north along the route to the Fezzan and Tripoli, and Islam linked them to North Africa and Mecca; later mais made the pilgrimage. In the 13th century Mai Dunama Dibbalemi built a large empire. Attacks by the Bulala drove the dynasty west to Bornu in the 14th century, where it rose again as Kanem-Bornu. The Sayfawa ruled for some 800 years, one of the longest dynasties anywhere. See also the trans-Saharan trade.
sum: The conversion of the rulers of Kanem, north and east of Lake Chad, to Islam in the late 11th century, under the king Hummay, founder of the Sayfawa dynasty.
